items.q: According to Kotter and Schlesinger, which reason for resistance to change best describes a situation where employees are concerned that the change will cost them their overtime pay?
opts: Parochial self-interest
Misunderstanding and lack of trust
Low tolerance of change
Different assessments of the situation
items.why: Parochial self-interest occurs when individuals prioritise their own personal gain or loss over the organisation's interests. Loss of overtime pay is a direct personal financial concern, fitting this category precisely. 'Different assessments' would apply if employees genuinely thought the change was a bad idea strategically, not because of personal loss.
items.label: New question

items.q: An employee resists change because it won't help her personally. The business offers her a role in managing the change. This is:
opts: Coercion to overcome fear
Coercion to overcome self-interest
Manipulation to overcome fear
Manipulation to overcome self-interest
items.why: The resistance is due to self-interest (won't help her personally). Offering a role to gain her cooperation is manipulation/co-option (giving her a desirable role to win her support without addressing the underlying concerns). Self-interest = 'what's – in it for me?' Offering a role is co-option (a form of manipulation) - giving them a stake in the change.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Statement 1: 'Market mapping is often used to calculate the market share of a business.' Statement 2: 'Market mapping shows the geographical location of a business on a map.'
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Both false. Market mapping plots products/brands on a grid based on two variables (e.g. price vs quality). It does not calculate market share or show geographical locations. Market mapping is confused with actual maps. It's a perceptual positioning tool.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Hartwell Foods produces both premium ready meals (YED = +1.8) and own-brand tinned soups (YED = −0.4). The UK economy enters a prolonged recession and average consumer incomes fall. Which of the following correctly predicts the combined effect on Hartwell Foods?
opts: Demand for both products will fall as consumers have less money to spend overall.
Demand for premium meals will fall and demand for tinned soups will rise.
Demand for premium meals will rise and demand for tinned soups will fall.
Demand for both products will rise because falling incomes increase the value consumers place on food.
items.why: A positive YED above 1 for premium meals means they are luxury goods — demand falls sharply as income falls. A negative YED for tinned soups means they are inferior goods — demand rises as income falls, since consumers trade down. This combination is a typical exam application of YED sign and magnitude.
items.label: New question

items.q: Statement 1: 'A prediction based on strong negative correlation has higher confidence than one based on weak positive correlation.' Statement 2: 'A business will base extrapolation on its qualitative market research.'
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Statement 1 true - correlation strength (strong vs weak) determines confidence, not direction. Confidence depends on strength, not direction.

items.q:
Consider the following statements about Handy's cultural types.

Statement 1: A role culture is most likely to be flexible and responsive to sudden changes in the external environment.
Statement 2: A power culture depends heavily on the values and decisions of one or a few individuals at the centre of the organisation.
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Role culture is built around rules, procedures and defined job roles; this rigidity makes it slow to respond to change, so Statement 1 is false. Power culture does depend on a central figure whose personality and judgement shapes the whole organisation, making Statement 2 true.
items.label: New question

items.q: Statement 1: 'Usually negative correlation between income changes and quantity demanded.' Statement 2: 'Usually positive correlation between competitor's price changes and quantity demanded.'
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Statement 1 false - for most (normal) goods, positive correlation between income and demand. Statement 2 true - competitor price rise = your demand rises (substitution). 'Usually' means most goods. Most are normal goods with positive income-demand correlation.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q:
Consider the following statements about network analysis.

Statement 1: Activities on the critical path have a total float of zero.
Statement 2: Reducing the duration of a non-critical activity will always shorten the overall project duration.
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Critical path activities have zero float by definition — any delay lengthens the project — so Statement 1 is true. Non-critical activities have float, meaning they can be shortened only up to the amount of float before they affect overall duration; cutting them further does not shorten the project unless they become the new critical path. Statement 2 is therefore false.
items.label: New question

items.q:
A manufacturing firm wants to introduce automated production lines. A force field analysis is carried out. Which of the following would be classified as a restraining force?

Statement 1: Workers fear redundancy and resist the change.
Statement 2: The automation is expected to reduce unit costs significantly.
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: A restraining force opposes change, so worker fear of redundancy is a restraining force (Statement 1 is true). Reduced unit costs is a benefit that drives the change forward, making it a driving force, not a restraining one (Statement 2 is false). Students often misread the direction of forces.
items.label: New question

items.q: In a network diagram, Activity D has an earliest start time of day 8 and a latest finish time of day 15. Activity D takes 5 days to complete. What is the total float of Activity D?
opts: 2 days
3 days
5 days
7 days
items.why: Total float = Latest finish time − Earliest start time − Duration = 15 − 8 − 5 = 2 days. Students commonly subtract only duration from latest finish, forgetting to account for the earliest start time, giving the wrong answer of 10 days, or they confuse total float with free float.
items.label: New question

items.q: A news report reveals that a major customer has cancelled a large contract with Oxton plc. All other things being equal, what is the most likely immediate effect on Oxton plc's share price?
opts: The share price will rise because the company's costs will fall.
The share price will fall because investors will revise expected future profits downward.
The share price will remain unchanged because share prices only change quarterly.
The share price will rise because the company can now focus on more profitable customers.
items.why: Share prices reflect investors' expectations of future profits and dividends. Loss of a major customer reduces expected future revenue and profit, causing investors to sell shares, which drives the price down. Share prices change continuously on a stock exchange, not quarterly.
items.label: New question

items.q: Airline: average CU = 74%, average passengers = 296. What is the plane capacity?
opts: 219 passengers
322 passengers
370 passengers
400 passengers
items.why: CU = actual/capacity x 100. So 74 = 296/capacity x 100. Capacity = 296/0.74 = 400 passengers. Rearrange the formula: Capacity = Actual output / CU rate. = 296 / 0.74 = 400.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Marton Flooring receives an order worth £90,000 in January. The customer will pay in March. Marton pays £40,000 for materials in January and £20,000 in wages in both January and February. What is Marton's net cash flow in February?
opts: £50,000 inflow, calculated by deducting the £40,000 materials payment made in January from the £90,000 customer receipt expected in March, then adjusting for the February wage cost
£70,000 outflow, representing the total of the £40,000 materials cost and the £20,000 February wages, offset against a proportion of the anticipated £90,000 receipt
−£20,000 (net outflow of £20,000)
£0, because the £20,000 wages paid in February are exactly cancelled out by an equivalent accrual of revenue relating to work completed during the month
items.why: In February, the only cash movement is the wage payment of £20,000 — there are no inflows (the customer pays in March, not February). Net cash flow in February is therefore −£20,000. Students often include the January materials cost or the March receipt in the February column.
items.label: New question

items.q: Fixed costs decrease, variable costs per unit increase, total costs at 100 units unchanged (point X). What happens?
opts: Break-even falls and margin of safety increases
Break-even increases and margin of safety falls
Break-even and margin of safety remain the same
Break-even remains the same, margin of safety increases
items.why: Lower FC means the total cost line starts lower at zero output. Higher VC per unit means the TC line is steeper. Since the total at 100 units is the same, the lines must cross the revenue line at a lower output (earlier break-even). Lower break-even with same actual output = higher margin of safety. The TC line pivots: lower start point (less FC) but steeper slope (more VC). This means it crosses revenue earlier = lower break-even.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Delayering in a business is likely to:
opts: decrease the span of control of managers.
improve the speed of vertical communication.
increase opportunities for promotion.
lead to less autonomy for workers.
items.why: Delayering removes management layers, making the hierarchy flatter. This speeds UP vertical communication because messages pass through fewer levels. Span of control widens (not decreases). Promotion opportunities decrease (fewer levels). Workers typically get more autonomy. Delayering: fewer layers = wider spans of control, faster communication, fewer promotion opportunities, more autonomy for workers.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: What is the latest finish time for Activity F?
opts: Day 7
Day 8
Day 10
Day 11
items.why: The latest finish time (lft) for Activity F is calculated by working backwards from the project end date. Based on the network, Activity F must be completed by Day 11 at the latest without delaying the project. lft = work backwards from project end. eft = work forwards from project start.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: A business must be at break-even if:
opts: Total contribution = fixed costs
Total contribution = total variable costs
Total profit = total costs
Total revenue = fixed costs
items.why: At break-even: profit = 0. Since Profit = Total Contribution - FC, when profit = 0, Total Contribution = Fixed Costs. This is the definition of break-even. Break-even = zero profit. Total Contribution = FC is the same as saying total revenue covers all costs exactly.

items.q:
Ferndale Foods is introducing a new stock management system. Managers are aware that some staff distrust senior leadership and do not fully understand why the change is necessary. Which method of overcoming resistance is most appropriate?

Statement 1: Facilitation and support is the most appropriate method because staff lack the skills to use the new system.
Statement 2: Education and communication is the most appropriate method because resistance stems from misunderstanding and lack of trust.
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: The scenario identifies misunderstanding and lack of trust as the cause of resistance; Kotter and Schlesinger prescribe education and communication for this cause, making Statement 2 true. Statement 1 is false because facilitation and support addresses anxiety and skill gaps, not distrust. There is no mention of skill deficiency here.
items.label: New question

items.q: Which source of finance is primarily for SHORT-TERM uses?
opts: Debt factoring
Share capital
Sale of buildings
Venture capital
items.why: Debt factoring provides immediate cash by selling receivables at a discount - it's a short-term cash flow solution. Share capital, building sales, and venture capital are all long-term sources. Debt factoring converts credit sales into immediate cash. It's specifically designed for short-term cash flow needs.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Which of the following is an example of disruptive, externally driven change rather than incremental, internally driven change?
opts: A retailer gradually rolling out a new staff appraisal scheme across its stores, responding to internal pressure from HR managers who identified weaknesses in performance management
A manufacturer introducing a continuous improvement programme to reduce waste, driven by internal targets set by the operations department following a review of production efficiency
A travel agency restructuring its business model after a new law banning short-haul flights is passed
A bank updating its internal HR software to a newer version as part of a planned technology refresh recommended by its in-house IT team
items.why: New legislation is an external shock that forces a fundamental rethink of the business model — this is disruptive, externally driven change. The other options all describe gradual, planned, internally initiated changes. Students sometimes confuse the scale of internal change with external disruption.
